title: Automated Emergency Triage for Remote Field Clinics
business: Remote medical field clinics operating in low-connectivity, high-stress environments.
problem: Medical staff in remote areas often face critical delays when manually documenting patient symptoms while simultaneously performing life-saving procedures, leading to incomplete triage records and potential diagnostic errors.
solution: By integrating GPT-Realtime-1.5, clinics can deploy a hands-free voice agent that listens to patient-provider interactions in real-time. The model processes raw audio input to generate structured clinical notes and immediate triage recommendations, allowing providers to maintain focus on the patient rather than data entry.
steps: Establish a persistent WebSocket connection to the v1/realtime endpoint to stream raw audio from the clinic environment.
Configure the session to utilize function_calling to trigger external medical database lookups based on detected symptoms.
Enable prompt_caching for standardized medical protocols to reduce latency during high-frequency triage sessions.
Process the model output as audio to provide immediate, synthesized guidance back to the field clinician.
outcome: Clinicians achieve higher focus on patient care, resulting in more comprehensive and accurate triage documentation generated concurrently with the examination.
limitation: The model relies on continuous audio streaming; network jitter or packet loss in remote areas can interrupt the session. To check for this, developers must monitor the WebSocket connection state and implement local audio buffering to ensure the model receives a coherent stream.
